testName: IISER IAT Mock Test: Ray Optics and Optical Instruments

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. What is the position and nature of the image formed?
options: 10 cm behind the mirror, virtual and erect
10 cm in front of the mirror, real and inverted
30 cm behind the mirror, virtual and erect
20 cm in front of the mirror, real and inverted
questions.explanation: Using the mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. For a convex mirror, f is positive (+15 cm). Object distance u = -30 cm. Substituting: 1/v + 1/(-30) = 1/15 ⇒ 1/v = 1/15 + 1/30 = 2/30 + 1/30 = 3/30 = 1/10. Therefore, v = +10 cm. A positive image distance for a mirror means the image forms behind it, rendering it virtual and erect.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction
questions.question: A bird in the air looks directly downwards at a fish swimming in a pond. The fish is at an actual depth of 12 cm below the water surface. If the refractive index of water is 4/3, at what apparent depth does the bird see the fish?
questions.explanation: When an object in a denser medium is viewed from a rarer medium normally, its apparent depth d' is given by d' = d / μ. Substituting the given values: d' = 12 / (4/3) = 12 × (3/4) = 9 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: Two thin lenses, one with a power of +4 D and another with a power of -2 D, are placed in close physical contact. What is the effective focal length of this optical combination?
questions.explanation: The equivalent power of thin lenses in contact is P = P₁ + P₂. Here, P = +4 D - 2 D = +2 D. The focal length is f = 1/P = 1/2 meters. Converting to centimeters, f = 50 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction through a prism
questions.question: A thin glass prism having a refracting angle of 5° produces a minimum angle of deviation of 2.5° for a monochromatic light ray. What is the refractive index of the prism material?
questions.explanation: For a thin prism, the minimum deviation δ is given by δ = (μ - 1)A. Given δ = 2.5° and A = 5°. Substituting the values: 2.5° = (μ - 1) × 5° ⇒ (μ - 1) = 2.5 / 5 = 0.5. Therefore, μ = 1 + 0.5 = 1.5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Total internal reflection
questions.question: Based on the provided diagram of the optical fiber, what is the critical angle for total internal reflection at the core-cladding interface?
questions.explanation: The critical angle C for total internal reflection is derived from Snell's law: sin C = μ_rarer / μ_denser. Here, the ray travels from the core (denser, μ₁ = 1.6) to the cladding (rarer, μ₂ = 1.2). Therefore, sin C = 1.2 / 1.6 = 12 / 16 = 3/4. The critical angle is C = sin⁻¹(3/4).
questions.imagePrompt: A schematic diagram of a step-index optical fiber. A light ray traveling inside the inner core (labeled μ₁ = 1.6) strikes the boundary with the outer cladding (labeled μ₂ = 1.2) at an angle θ to the normal. The ray is shown undergoing total internal reflection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Optical instruments
questions.question: An astronomical telescope in normal adjustment (final image at infinity) has a magnifying power of 10. If the focal length of the eyepiece is 2 cm, what is the focal length of the objective lens?
questions.explanation: The magnifying power of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is M = f_o / f_e. Given M = 10 and f_e = 2 cm. 10 = f_o / 2 ⇒ f_o = 20 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A solid glass rod (μ = 1.5) has a convex hemispherical end of radius curvature 5 cm. A point object is placed in the air on the principal axis at a distance of 20 cm from the pole of the hemispherical surface. At what distance from the pole is the image formed inside the glass?
questions.explanation: Formula for refraction at a single spherical surface: μ₂/v - μ₁/u = (μ₂ - μ₁)/R. Object is in air (μ₁ = 1), image in glass (μ₂ = 1.5). Surface is convex towards the rarer medium, so R = +5 cm. Object distance u = -20 cm. Substituting: 1.5/v - 1/(-20) = (1.5 - 1)/5 ⇒ 1.5/v + 0.05 = 0.5/5 = 0.1. Thus, 1.5/v = 0.1 - 0.05 = 0.05. v = 1.5 / 0.05 = +30 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A biconvex lens made of glass (μ_g = 1.5) has radii of curvature R₁ = 10 cm and R₂ = 15 cm. What will be its new focal length if it is completely immersed in water (μ_w = 4/3)?
questions.explanation: First, find focal length in air (f_a): 1/f_a = (μ_g - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = (1.5 - 1)(1/10 - 1/(-15)) = 0.5(3/30 + 2/30) = 0.5(5/30) = 1/12 ⇒ f_a = 12 cm. For focal length in liquid (f_w), use the ratio shortcut: f_w / f_a = (μ_g - 1) / (μ_g/μ_w - 1). Here, μ_g/μ_w = 1.5 / (4/3) = 9/8. Ratio = 0.5 / (9/8 - 1) = 0.5 / 0.125 = 4. Therefore, f_w = 4 × f_a = 4 × 12 = 48 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction through a prism
questions.question: An equilateral glass prism is set in the position of minimum deviation for a specific wavelength of light. The angle of minimum deviation is observed to be exactly equal to the angle of the prism. What is the refractive index of the prism material?
questions.explanation: The refractive index is given by μ = sin((A + δ_m)/2) / sin(A/2). For an equilateral prism, A = 60°. Given that δ_m = A = 60°. Substitute these values: μ = sin((60° + 60°)/2) / sin(60°/2) = sin(60°) / sin(30°) = (√3/2) / (1/2) = √3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Optical instruments
questions.question: A compound microscope has an objective lens of focal length 1 cm and an eyepiece of focal length 5 cm. The distance between the focal point of the objective and the focal point of the eyepiece (the optical tube length L) is 20 cm. What is the approximate magnifying power of the microscope when the final image is formed at the least distance of distinct vision (D = 25 cm)?
questions.explanation: The approximate formula for the magnifying power of a compound microscope is M ≈ (L / f_o) × (1 + D / f_e). Given L = 20 cm, f_o = 1 cm, D = 25 cm, f_e = 5 cm. M = (20 / 1) × (1 + 25/5) = 20 × (1 + 5) = 20 × 6 = 120.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: A highly polished concave mirror forms a sharp, real image of a point object on a screen. If the upper half of the mirror's reflecting surface is painted completely black, what will happen to the image on the screen?
options: The top half of the image disappears.
The bottom half of the image disappears.
The entire image remains intact, but its intensity is halved.
questions.explanation: Every small section of a spherical mirror independently focuses rays to create the full image. Covering half the mirror does not block half the image; it simply blocks half the light rays from reaching the focal point. Consequently, the entire image is still formed, but its brightness (intensity) is reduced by half.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Total internal reflection
questions.question: What is the minimum radius R of the floating opaque disc required to completely prevent light from the coin from emerging into the air above?
questions.explanation: To prevent light from escaping, the disc must cover the area where rays hit the surface at angles less than the critical angle C. The radius is R = h tan C. First, find sin C = 1/μ = 1 / (5/4) = 4/5. Using a right triangle (opposite=4, hypotenuse=5), adjacent = √(5² - 4²) = 3. Therefore, tan C = 4/3. R = 4 m × (4/3) = 16/3 m ≈ 5.33 m.
questions.imagePrompt: A diagram showing a bright coin resting at the flat bottom of a pool of water of depth h = 4 m. The refractive index of water is given as μ = 5/4. Directly above the coin, a circular opaque disc of radius R floats on the water surface, perfectly blocking all light rays originating from the coin from escaping into the air.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: In an optics lab, a student uses the displacement method to determine the focal length of a convex lens. The fixed distance between the illuminated object and the viewing screen is 90 cm. Sharp images of the object are obtained on the screen for two distinct positions of the lens, which are separated by a distance of 30 cm. What is the focal length of this lens?
questions.explanation: The focal length f in the displacement method is given by f = (D² - x²) / 4D, where D is the distance between object and screen, and x is the separation between the two lens positions. Here D = 90 cm, x = 30 cm. f = (90² - 30²) / (4 × 90) = (8100 - 900) / 360 = 7200 / 360 = 20 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: A thin convex lens made of optical glass with a refractive index of 1.5 has a focal length f in air. If this lens is completely immersed in a transparent liquid medium that also has a refractive index of 1.5, what will its effective focal length become?
questions.explanation: The Lens Maker's formula states 1/f = (μ_lens/μ_medium - 1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂). When the lens is immersed in a liquid with the same refractive index, μ_lens / μ_medium = 1.5 / 1.5 = 1. Thus, the first term (1 - 1) becomes zero. 1/f = 0, which means f = Infinity. The lens no longer bends light and behaves like a simple plane glass plate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Reflection of light by spherical mirrors
questions.question: Two plane mirrors are inclined to each other at an angle of 60°. A ray of light is incident on the first mirror, traveling exactly parallel to the second mirror. After two consecutive reflections (one from each mirror), the ray emerges traveling exactly parallel to the first mirror. What is the total angle of deviation suffered by the ray?
questions.explanation: The total deviation δ suffered by a ray undergoing two reflections between two plane mirrors inclined at an angle θ is independent of the angle of incidence. It is given by the formula δ = 360° - 2θ. Given θ = 60°, δ = 360° - 2(60°) = 360° - 120° = 240°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question:
Passage: A specialized biconvex lens is manufactured by fusing two different optical materials together horizontally along the principal axis. The top half is made of material with μ₁ = 1.5, and the bottom half with μ₂ = 1.6. Radii of curvature are R₁ = R₂ = 20 cm. A point object is placed at u = -30 cm on the principal axis.

How many distinct images of the point object will be formed by this composite lens?
questions.explanation: The lens is horizontally split, creating a top half and a bottom half. Because the refractive indices (μ₁ and μ₂) are different, the Lens Maker's formula will yield two different focal lengths for the upper and lower sections. Rays passing through the top half converge to one point, while rays through the bottom half converge to a different point. Thus, exactly 2 distinct images are formed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: Passage Continued: What is the absolute distance separating the distinct images formed by the upper and lower halves of this composite lens?
questions.explanation:
Calculate f for top half (μ₁=1.5): 1/f₁ = (1.5-1)(1/20 - (-1/20)) = 0.5(2/20) = 1/20 ⇒ f₁ = 20 cm. 
Calculate f for bottom half (μ₂=1.6): 1/f₂ = (1.6-1)(2/20) = 0.6/10 = 6/100 ⇒ f₂ = 100/6 = 16.67 cm.
Find v₁: 1/v₁ - 1/(-30) = 1/20 ⇒ 1/v₁ = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60 ⇒ v₁ = 60 cm.
Find v₂: 1/v₂ - 1/(-30) = 6/100 ⇒ 1/v₂ = 18/300 - 10/300 = 8/300 ⇒ v₂ = 300/8 = 37.5 cm.
Both images lie on the principal axis. The distance separating them is |60 - 37.5| = 22.5 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction at spherical surfaces and by lenses
questions.question: What is the effective focal length of this silvered lens system when used to form an image of an object placed in front of the flat surface?
questions.explanation:
A silvered lens acts as a mirror with equivalent power P_eq = 2P_L + P_M. 
Power of lens P_L = (μ-1)(1/R₁ - 1/R₂) = (1.5-1)(1/∞ - 1/(-20)) = 0.5(1/20) = 1/40 cm⁻¹. 
Light hits the convex surface from inside, meaning the silvering acts as a concave mirror: f_M = -R/2 = -10 cm. Power of mirror P_M = -1/f_M = +1/10 cm⁻¹. 
P_eq = 2(1/40) + 1/10 = 1/20 + 1/10 = 3/20 cm⁻¹. 
Effective focal length F = -1/P_eq = -20/3 cm ≈ -6.67 cm.
questions.imagePrompt: A plano-convex lens made of glass (μ=1.5) rests horizontally. Its flat surface faces the left, and its convex curved surface (radius R=20 cm) faces the right. The curved convex surface is heavily silvered, indicated by metallic shading, turning it into a reflecting boundary. Light enters from the left through the flat face.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction
questions.question: A solid glass slab of thickness 6 cm and refractive index 1.5 is placed directly in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The flat faces of the slab are perpendicular to the principal axis of the mirror. A point object is placed on the principal axis at a distance of 21 cm from the pole of the mirror, with the slab located entirely between the object and the mirror. Where is the final image formed by the system located relative to the pole of the mirror?
options: 19.11 cm in front of the mirror
21.11 cm in front of the mirror
23.11 cm in front of the mirror
17.11 cm in front of the mirror
questions.explanation:
1. Slab shifts object toward mirror: s = t(1 - 1/μ) = 6(1 - 2/3) = 2 cm. Apparent u = -(21 - 2) = -19 cm.
2. Mirror reflection: 1/v + 1/(-19) = 1/(-10) ⇒ 1/v = 1/19 - 1/10 = -9/190. Image forms at v = -21.11 cm.
3. The reflected rays travel back through the slab, away from the mirror. The slab shifts the image again by 2 cm in the direction of light (away from the mirror). 
Final position = 21.11 + 2 = 23.11 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Refraction through a prism
questions.question: An achromatic doublet is constructed by combining two thin prisms, A and B, in opposition to produce dispersion without deviation for the mean yellow light. Prism A has an angle A₁ = 6° and is made of crown glass with refractive indices μ_v1=1.52, μ_r1=1.48, μ_y1=1.50. Prism B is made of flint glass with refractive indices μ_v2=1.63, μ_r2=1.57, μ_y2=1.60. What is the magnitude of the net angular dispersion produced by this prism combination?
